claim: RNF213 is the major susceptibility factor for Moyamoya disease.
source: RNF213 is the major susceptibility factor for Moyamoya disease, a progressive cerebrovascular disorder that often leads to brain stroke in adults and children.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and introduction, supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Moyamoya disease is a progressive cerebrovascular disorder that often leads to brain stroke in adults and children.
source: RNF213 is the major susceptibility factor for Moyamoya disease, a progressive cerebrovascular disorder that often leads to brain stroke in adults and children.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge about the disease.

claim: Mouse RNF213 is a 584 kDa protein comprising 5148 residues.
source: Consistent with this, the full-length mouse RNF213 (584 kDa, 5148 residues) analyzed in the present study is a stable protein that could be efficiently produced in insect cells and analyzed by single-particle cryo-EM (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is directly stated in the Results section describing the protein studied.

claim: RNF213 has overall dimensions of 90 × 130 × 220 Å³.
source: The initial cryo-EM class averages revealed a compact macromolecule with overall dimensions of 90 × 130 × 220 Å3, depicting the RNF213 ubiquitin ligase in its monomeric state.
evidence: This measurement is derived from cryo-EM analysis of the protein.

claim: RNF213 exists as a monomer in solution.
source: Size exclusion chromatography (SEC) and dynamic light scattering (DLS) analyses pointed to a monodisperse protein population (Figure 1bc), suggesting that the monomer is the dominant form of RNF213 in solution.
evidence: This is supported by SEC and DLS experimental data shown in Figure 1bc.

claim: The cryo-EM structure of wildtype RNF213 was resolved at an average resolution of 3.2 Å.
source: The final atomic models of wildtype (wt) RNF213 and the R4753K MMD mutant comprise residues 476–5148, contain >80% of all side chains and were resolved at an average resolution of 3.2 Å and 3.1 Å, respectively, with the best-refined regions reaching 2.8 Å (Figure 1—figure supplement 2, Table 1).
evidence: This resolution is reported from the cryo-EM structure determination.

claim: The cryo-EM structure of R4753K RNF213 mutant was resolved at an average resolution of 3.1 Å.
source: The final atomic models of wildtype (wt) RNF213 and the R4753K MMD mutant comprise residues 476–5148, contain >80% of all side chains and were resolved at an average resolution of 3.2 Å and 3.1 Å, respectively, with the best-refined regions reaching 2.8 Å (Figure 1—figure supplement 2, Table 1).
evidence: This resolution is reported from the cryo-EM structure determination.

claim: RNF213 comprises an N-terminal stalk, a dynein-like core with six ATPase units, and a multidomain E3 module.
source: The structure reveals the intricate fold of the 584 kDa protein, comprising an N-terminal stalk, a dynein-like core with six ATPase units, and a multidomain E3 module.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by the structural analysis presented.

claim: RNF213 is organized into three structural components: N-arm, AAA, and E3 module.
source: Its intricate protein fold arranges 20 sub-domains in a zig-zag meandering manner into three structural components, to which we refer as N-arm, AAA, and E3 module (Figure 1, Video 3).
evidence: This is directly stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1.

claim: The N-arm of RNF213 comprises residues 1-1290.
source: The N-arm (residues 1–1290) is composed of a disordered region followed by a string of helical bundles that yield a 180 Å-long stalk leaning against the AAA and E3 portions.
evidence: This is stated in the structural description of RNF213.

claim: The N-arm forms a 180 Å-long stalk.
source: The N-arm (residues 1–1290) is composed of a disordered region followed by a string of helical bundles that yield a 180 Å-long stalk leaning against the AAA and E3 portions.
evidence: This measurement is derived from the cryo-EM structure.

claim: The AAA core of RNF213 is composed of six non-equivalent AAA units spanning residues 1775-3405.
source: A linker (1291–1774) connects the N-arm to the second module, the AAA core, which is composed of six non-equivalent AAA units (1775–3405, AAA1 to AAA6).
evidence: This is stated in the structural description.

claim: The E3 module of RNF213 comprises residues 3589-4926.
source: This E3 module (3589–4926) is composed of a heart-shaped, 4-domain scaffold that positions the E3-RING (3940–3999) at the edge of the RNF213 molecule, opposite to the AAA core.
evidence: This is stated in the structural description.

claim: The E3-RING domain spans residues 3940-3999.
source: This E3 module (3589–4926) is composed of a heart-shaped, 4-domain scaffold that positions the E3-RING (3940–3999) at the edge of the RNF213 molecule, opposite to the AAA core.
evidence: This is stated in the structural description.

claim: RNF213 is the closest structural homolog to dynein.
source: As such, RNF213 is equivalent to dynein, which was found to be the closest structural homolog of RNF213 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated based on structural comparison analysis.

claim: Only AAA3 and AAA4 of RNF213 are catalytically competent ATPase domains.
source: Analysis of individual ATPase motifs revealed that in RNF213 only AAA3 and AAA4 are catalytically competent, bearing all functional motifs (Figure 2b).
evidence: This is based on analysis of conserved ATPase motifs in the structure.

claim: AAA2 of RNF213 contains a bound ATP molecule.
source: Moreover, the cryo-EM density unambiguously revealed a co-purified ATP molecule that is bound to AAA2 (Figure 2a, Video 2).
evidence: This is directly observed in the cryo-EM density map.

claim: AAA2 of RNF213 lacks catalytic residues required for ATP hydrolysis.
source: Consistent with the unexpected density, AAA2 contains a proper nucleotide binding site, but lacks catalytic residues (Walker B, sensor I) required for ATP hydrolysis.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of the AAA2 active site.

claim: The IR3 insertion (residues 2487-2538) in AAA3 functions as a molecular wedge separating AAA3 and AAA4.
source: First, AAA3L harbors a 51-residue loop (IR3, 2487–2538) that protrudes in a well-defined conformation to the adjacent AAA4. The cryo-EM structure suggests that this RNF213 signature motif functions as a molecular wedge, separating AAA3 and AAA4.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural position and conformation of IR3.

claim: The IR5 insertion (residues 3063-3103) in AAA5 sterically blocks nucleotide binding to AAA4.
source: Second, AAA5L contains a 40-residue insertion (IR5, 3063–3103) forming an αβ3 structure at the AAA4/AAA5 interface. At the edge of IR5, Tyr3078 reaches over toward the active site of AAA4, sterically blocking nucleotide binding (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is observed in the cryo-EM structure showing Tyr3078 blocking the AAA4 active site.

claim: The IR3 and IR5 insertions should hinder nucleotide binding to AAA3 and AAA4, diminishing RNF213 ATPase activity.
source: Together, the two insertions IR3 and IR5, which are amongst the most conserved RNF213 protein stretches (Figure 2—figure supplement 2c), should hinder nucleotide binding to AAA3 and AAA4, diminishing RNF213 ATPase activity.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural positions of IR3 and IR5 and their conservation.

claim: The current cryo-EM structure reflects the auto-inhibited form of the RNF213 ATPase.
source: We thus presume that the current cryo-EM structure reflects the auto-inhibited form of the RNF213 ATPase.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural features showing inhibitory elements.

claim: A 20 Å gap between AAA6 and AAA1 divides the AAA hexamer into two halves.
source: A 20 Å gap between AAA6 and AAA1 divides the hexamer into two halves, AAA1/2/3 and AAA4/5/6, which may reorient en-bloc upon nucleotide-dependent structural changes in AAA3 and AAA4.
evidence: This is observed in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: RNF213 matches best to the resting states of dynein (phi-particle and apo form).
source: Detailed structural comparisons revealed that RNF213 matches best to the resting states of dynein – the phi-particle (Zhang et al., 2017) and the apo form (Schmidt et al., 2012; Figure 2c, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on structural alignment and comparison with dynein structures.

claim: AAA1 of RNF213 lacks Walker A and Walker B motifs.
source: In contrast, AAA1 of RNF213 lacks Walker A and Walker B motifs altogether and should be incapable of binding and hydrolyzing ATP and functioning as processive motor.
evidence: This is based on sequence and structural analysis of AAA1.

claim: The ATPase activity of RNF213 is an order of magnitude lower than that of a processive AAA machine.
source: Consistent with this, we observed that the ATPase activity of RNF213 is an order of magnitude lower than that of a processive AAA machine (Figure 2d).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the ATPase assay data shown in Figure 2d.

claim: The basal ATPase activity of RNF213 is approximately 3-fold lower than that of dynein at rest.
source: Moreover, the basal activity of RNF213 is ~3 fold lower than that of dynein at rest, pointing to an additional inhibitory element controlling AAA activity, as predicted by the cryo-EM structure.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the ATPase assay comparing RNF213 and dynein.

claim: The E3-RING domain contains a C4HC3 motif coordinating two Zn²⁺ ions in a cross-braced arrangement.
source: The E3-RING, inserted between the two ultimate helices of the E3-back, contains a C4HC3 motif coordinating two Zn2+ ions in a cross-braced arrangement (Metzger et al., 2014).
evidence: This is observed in the cryo-EM structure and is consistent with known RING domain structures.

claim: In RNF213, the conserved Lys/Arg linchpin residue is replaced by a Leu.
source: In RNF213, however, the Lys/Arg linchpin is replaced by a Leu (Figure 3b), a hydrophobic residue that is unlikely to stabilize the reactive E2 ~Ub intermediate (Koliopoulos et al., 2016; Pruneda et al., 2012).
evidence: This is observed in the structure and compared to canonical RING E3 ligases.

claim: UbcH7 is the most efficient E2 enzyme for enabling RNF213 ubiquitin transfer activity.
source: To this end, we performed an E2 screen testing 34 ubiquitin-conjugating enzymes and observed that UbcH7 is most efficient in enabling the Ub transfer activity. The stimulated activity was in this case even 2–3 times higher than with UbcH5 variants, which are promiscuous E2 enzymes working with many E3 ligases (Figure 3c).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the E2 screen assay shown in Figure 3c.

claim: UbcH7 is reactive only with cysteine residues and works with transthiolation E3 enzymes such as HECT, RBR, and RCR ubiquitin ligases.
source: This finding is surprising, because UbcH7 is not known to collaborate with canonical RING-type E3s as it lacks intrinsic reactivity with lysine. Instead, UbcH7 is reactive only with cysteine residues and works together with transthiolation E3 enzymes such as HECT (Schwarz et al., 1998), RBR (Wenzel et al., 2011), and RCR (Pao et al., 2018) ubiquitin ligases.
evidence: This is stated based on established knowledge about UbcH7 and cited literature.

claim: RNF213 was identified as one of the most prominent E3 ligases collaborating with UbcH7 in an E3 proteomics analysis.
source: Support for the here proposed cysteine-dependent ubiquitination activity of RNF213 stems from a recent E3 proteomics analysis (Pao et al., 2018). Using an activity-based E2 probe, RNF213 was identified as one of the most prominent E3 ligases collaborating with UbcH7, outranking its established partner enzymes, such as LUBAC, PARKIN, and HERC2.
evidence: This is cited from a published proteomics study.

claim: The ΔRING mutant of RNF213 exhibited wildtype-like auto-ubiquitination activity with either UbcH7 or UbcH5c.
source: Strikingly, ΔRING exhibited wt-like auto-ubiquitination activity with either UbcH7 or UbcH5c (Figure 3d, Figure 3—figure supplement 1), indicating that the RING itself is not involved in the ubiquitin transfer.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the auto-ubiquitination assay comparing wt and ΔRING mutant.

claim: The RING domain is not involved in the ubiquitin transfer reaction of RNF213.
source: Strikingly, ΔRING exhibited wt-like auto-ubiquitination activity with either UbcH7 or UbcH5c (Figure 3d, Figure 3—figure supplement 1), indicating that the RING itself is not involved in the ubiquitin transfer.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the functional activity of the ΔRING mutant.

claim: The E3 subdomains (E3-back, E3-shell, E3-core, and CTD) do not have counterparts in the PDB database.
source: On top of that, a DALI search for structural homologs revealed that the E3 subdomains – namely the E3-back, the E3-shell, the E3-core, and the CTD – do not have counterparts in the PDB database.
evidence: This is based on a DALI structural homology search.

claim: RNF213 shares no similarity to any known E3 ligase on either the sequence or structural level.
source: The active ΔRING mutant therefore shares no similarity to any known E3 ligase either on the sequence or on the structural level, suggesting that RNF213 employs a yet undescribed E3 scaffold to perform its ubiquitin ligase function in a RING-independent manner.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural analysis and functional data.

claim: Wildtype and R4753K RNF213 proteins have an almost identical structure with an rms deviation of 0.69 Å for 4308 Cα atoms.
source: Cryo-EM analysis of the equivalent R4753K mutation in mouse RNF213 indicated that wt and R4753K proteins have an almost identical structure and can be aligned with a root mean square (rms) deviation of 0.69 Å for 4308 Cα atoms.
evidence: This is based on structural comparison of the two cryo-EM structures.

claim: Arg4753 is located at the end of an α-helix, fastening the ends of an 'omega' structure formed by residues 4750-4809.
source: Arg4753 is located at the end of an α-helix, fastening the ends of an 'omega' structure formed by residues 4750–4809 (Figure 4a).
evidence: This is observed in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: Asp4806 undergoes close interactions with Arg4753.
source: Asp4806, the partner residue on the opposite flank of this motif, undergoes close interactions with Arg4753, as directly seen in the cryo-EM density (Figure 4b).
evidence: This is directly observed in the cryo-EM density map.

claim: The R4753K mutation disrupts the salt bridge between Arg4753 and Asp4806.
source: The R4753K mutation disrupts this salt bridge, weakening the sealing of the omega motif and leading to small but significant structural adaptations in its immediate environment (Figure 4b).
evidence: This is observed by comparing the wt and R4753K cryo-EM structures.

claim: Mutation of Asp4806 is also associated with Moyamoya disease.
source: Interestingly, mutating the Arg4753 partner residue Asp4806 is also associated with MMD (Liu et al., 2011), highlighting the relevance of the identified structural motif.
evidence: This is cited from published literature on MMD mutations.

claim: The R4753K MMD founder mutation does not significantly alter the enzymatic properties of RNF213 in vitro.
source: These data indicated that the MMD founder mutation, though causing local structural changes, does not significantly alter the enzymatic properties of RNF213 in vitro (Figure 2d, Figure 4c).
evidence: This is demonstrated by ATPase and ubiquitination assays comparing wt and R4753K.

claim: The penetrance of R4753K in Moyamoya disease is low, with only 1 in 200 carriers developing disease.
source: Consistent with the minor structural and functional effects, the penetrance of R4753K in MMD is low, as only 1 from 200 carriers develops disease (Liu et al., 2011).
evidence: This is cited from published literature on MMD epidemiology.

claim: 21 out of 28 severe RNF213 mutations (CADD-score >20) are localized in one of the four E3 sub-domains.
source: This plot reveals that MMD mutations strongly cluster in the E3 module, with 21 out of 28 severe RNF213 mutations (CADD-score >20) localized in one of its four E3 sub-domains (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is based on mapping MMD mutations onto the structure and analyzing their CADD scores.

claim: The mutations with the highest predicted pathogenicity are located at the subdomain interfaces of the E3 module.
source: Remarkably, the mutations with the highest predicted pathogenicity are located at the subdomain interfaces and should alter the overall conformation and dynamics of the composite E3 module, and thus its ubiquitination activity.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural positions of high-CADD score mutations.

claim: At least 16 million people in East Asia are carriers of RNF213 mutations.
source: MMD is most prevalent in East Asia, where at least 16 million people are carriers of RNF213 mutations, with onset of disease in >50,000 cases (Liu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is cited from published epidemiological data.

claim: More than 50,000 cases of Moyamoya disease have onset in East Asia.
source: MMD is most prevalent in East Asia, where at least 16 million people are carriers of RNF213 mutations, with onset of disease in >50,000 cases (Liu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is cited from published epidemiological data.

claim: RNF213 plays an important role in lipid metabolism modulating lipotoxicity.
source: It was shown that RNF213 plays an important role in lipid metabolism modulating lipotoxicity (Piccolis et al., 2019), fat storage, and lipid droplet formation (Sugihara et al., 2019).
evidence: This is cited from published studies on RNF213 function.

claim: RNF213 plays a role in fat storage and lipid droplet formation.
source: It was shown that RNF213 plays an important role in lipid metabolism modulating lipotoxicity (Piccolis et al., 2019), fat storage, and lipid droplet formation (Sugihara et al., 2019).
evidence: This is cited from published studies on RNF213 function.

claim: RNF213 together with PTP1B and HIF1A coordinates the cellular response to hypoxia, controlling non-mitochondrial oxygen consumption.
source: Moreover, RNF213 together with PTP1B and HIF1A coordinates the cellular response to hypoxia, controlling non-mitochondrial oxygen consumption (Banh et al., 2016).
evidence: This is cited from published studies on RNF213 function.

claim: RNF213 knock-down causes gross changes in the ubiquitome, particularly of members of the NF-κB pathway.
source: Proteomic searches for cellular targets revealed a connection to the ubiquitin-proteasome system, where RNF213 knock-down causes gross changes in the ubiquitome, in particular of members of the NF-κB pathway (Banh et al., 2016; Piccolis et al., 2019).
evidence: This is cited from published proteomic studies.

claim: RNF213 is capable of activating NF-κB signaling.
source: In fact, RNF213 is capable of activating NF-κB signaling and could thus, by inducing the expression of inflammatory cytokines such as interleukin-6, influence angiogenesis and MMD (Piccolis et al., 2019).
evidence: This is cited from published studies on RNF213 function.

claim: With a mass of 591 kDa, RNF213 is the largest E3 ubiquitin ligase in the human proteome.
source: Notably, with a mass of 591 kDa, RNF213 is the largest E3 ubiquitin ligase in the human proteome.
evidence: This is stated as a known fact about RNF213.

claim: RNF213 combines RING and AAA domains in a single polypeptide.
source: It combines RING and AAA (ATPase associated with a variety of cellular activities) domains in a single polypeptide, making it a unique E3 machine in the ubiquitination system.
evidence: This is stated based on the domain organization of RNF213.

claim: RNF213 is a highly conserved protein expressed in all vertebrates.
source: RNF213 is a highly conserved protein expressed in all vertebrates (Figure 1a, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is stated based on sequence conservation analysis shown in Figure 1a.

claim: The giant E3 ligase RNF213 is predicted to be a structured protein with few disordered regions.
source: Despite the lack of annotated domains for >4000 residues, the giant E3 ligase is predicted to be a structured protein with few disordered regions (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is based on FoldIndex prediction analysis.

claim: Full-length mouse RNF213 is a stable protein that could be efficiently produced in insect cells.
source: Consistent with this, the full-length mouse RNF213 (584 kDa, 5148 residues) analyzed in the present study is a stable protein that could be efficiently produced in insect cells and analyzed by single-particle cryo-EM (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the successful expression and purification of the protein.

claim: The individual components of RNF213 (N-arm, AAA, E3 module) were visualized at average resolutions of 3.4, 3.0, and 3.1 Å, respectively.
source: The individual components were visualized at an average resolution of 3.4, 3.0, and 3.1 Å, respectively.
evidence: This is reported from the focused refinement of different structural modules.

claim: A linker comprising residues 1291-1774 connects the N-arm to the AAA core.
source: A linker (1291–1774) connects the N-arm to the second module, the AAA core, which is composed of six non-equivalent AAA units (1775–3405, AAA1 to AAA6).
evidence: This is stated in the structural description.

claim: The hinge domain of RNF213 comprises residues 3406-3588.
source: The midpoint of the RNF213 molecule consists of the hinge domain (3406–3588), which connects the AAA core to the third module, harboring the ubiquitin ligase activity.
evidence: This is stated in the structural description.

claim: The E3 module is composed of a heart-shaped, 4-domain scaffold.
source: This E3 module (3589–4926) is composed of a heart-shaped, 4-domain scaffold that positions the E3-RING (3940–3999) at the edge of the RNF213 molecule, opposite to the AAA core.
evidence: This is observed in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: The CTD is a bilobal α-helical domain located at the AAA-E3 interface.
source: At its distal end, the E3 fold embraces a 20-residue loop that returns to the center of the molecule (Figure 1c), placing the CTD – a bilobal α-helical domain – at the AAA-E3 interface.
evidence: This is observed in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: RNF213 was previously proposed to form hexameric particles to yield the active AAA ATPase.
source: Of note, only two of the AAA domains had been identified in previous analyses, and given their homology to Hsp100 unfoldases, RNF213 was proposed to form hexameric particles to yield the active AAA ATPase (Morito et al., 2015).
evidence: This is cited from a previous publication.

claim: The present structure demonstrates that RNF213 encodes six AAA units within a single polypeptide chain.
source: Contrary to this, the present structure demonstrates that the protein encodes six AAA units within a single polypeptide chain.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the cryo-EM structure.

claim: AAA ATPase domains are composed of a large α/β (L) and a small α-helical (S) domain, with the nucleotide binding site located at their interface.
source: In general, AAA ATPase domains are composed of a large α/β (L) and a small α-helical (S) domain, with the nucleotide binding site located at their interface (Erzberger and Berger, 2006).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about AAA domains, supported by citation.

claim: The arginine finger is provided by the L-domain of the adjacent AAA unit, enabling signaling between AAA 'rigid bodies'.
source: While the L/S domains carry most motifs for ATP binding (Walker A) and hydrolysis (Walker B, sensor I/II), one critical catalytic residue, the arginine finger (RF), is provided by the L-domain of the adjacent AAA unit, enabling signaling between AAA 'rigid bodies' (Wang et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about AAA domains, supported by citation.

claim: Residues from both AAA2 and AAA3 tightly coordinate ATP, making the nucleotide a molecular glue tethering the two domains.
source: Instead, residues from both AAA2 and AAA3 tightly coordinate ATP, making the nucleotide a molecular glue tethering the two domains (Figure 2—figure supplement 2a).
evidence: This is observed in the cryo-EM structure of the AAA2 active site.

claim: Most RNF213-specific insertions have a structural role stabilizing the rigid bodies within the AAA ring.
source: Furthermore, comparison with canonical AAA hexamers revealed RNF213-specific insertions (Figure 2ab), most of which seem to have a structural role stabilizing the rigid bodies within the AAA ring.
evidence: This is inferred from structural comparison with canonical AAA hexamers.

claim: IR3 and IR5 are amongst the most conserved RNF213 protein stretches.
source: Together, the two insertions IR3 and IR5, which are amongst the most conserved RNF213 protein stretches (Figure 2—figure supplement 2c), should hinder nucleotide binding to AAA3 and AAA4, diminishing RNF213 ATPase activity.
evidence: This is shown by sequence conservation analysis in Figure 2—figure supplement 2c.

claim: The latent ATPase state of RNF213 is characterized by an opened AAA ring.
source: Our structural data suggest that the latent ATPase state is characterized by an opened AAA ring (Figure 2ab).
evidence: This is observed in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: A similar open-closed transition of the AAA ring has been observed for dynein.
source: A similar open-closed transition of the AAA ring has been observed for dynein (Bhabha et al., 2014; Schmidt et al., 2012).
evidence: This is cited from published dynein structures.

claim: The upstream linker domain adopts a similar fold and position above the RNF213 and dynein AAA rings.
source: Moreover, the upstream linker domain adopts a similar fold and position above the RNF213 and dynein AAA rings (Figure 2c), despite lacking any sequence similarity, and may therefore regulate ATPase function in an equivalent manner.
evidence: This is observed by structural comparison with dynein.

claim: In dynein, AAA1 is the most active ATPase driving processive movement along microtubules.
source: In dynein, AAA1 is the most active ATPase driving processive movement along microtubules (Kon et al., 2004; Reck-Peterson and Vale, 2004), while AAA3/AAA4 are proposed to function as a molecular switch turning the dynein motor on and off (Bhabha et al., 2014).
evidence: This is cited from published studies on dynein mechanism.

claim: In dynein, AAA3/AAA4 are proposed to function as a molecular switch turning the dynein motor on and off.
source: In dynein, AAA1 is the most active ATPase driving processive movement along microtubules (Kon et al., 2004; Reck-Peterson and Vale, 2004), while AAA3/AAA4 are proposed to function as a molecular switch turning the dynein motor on and off (Bhabha et al., 2014).
evidence: This is cited from published studies on dynein mechanism.

claim: The E3 module is composed of the E3-back, E3-shell, E3-core domains, and the CTD.
source: The ubiquitin ligase activity of RNF213 is expected to depend on the E3-RING domain, which is located on top of the E3 scaffold composed by the E3-back, E3-shell, and E3-core domains (Figure 1c, Figure 3a).
evidence: This is stated in the structural description and shown in figures.

claim: In RING/E2~Ub complexes, ubiquitin is covalently bound via a strained thioester to the E2, facilitating nucleophilic attack of a substrate's lysine residue.
source: In RING/E2 ~Ub complexes, ubiquitin is covalently bound via a strained thioester to the E2, facilitating nucleophilic attack of a substrate's lysine residue (Plechanovová et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about RING E3 mechanisms, supported by citation.

claim: The RING 'linchpin' is a conserved Lys/Arg residue that locks the E2 and Ub in the 'closed' conformation primed for catalysis.
source: Key for this lysine-reactivity is the RING 'linchpin', a conserved Lys/Arg residue that locks the E2 and Ub in the 'closed' conformation primed for catalysis (Pruneda et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about RING E3 mechanisms, supported by citation.

claim: A hydrophobic residue at the linchpin position is unlikely to stabilize the reactive E2~Ub intermediate.
source: In RNF213, however, the Lys/Arg linchpin is replaced by a Leu (Figure 3b), a hydrophobic residue that is unlikely to stabilize the reactive E2 ~Ub intermediate (Koliopoulos et al., 2016; Pruneda et al., 2012).
evidence: This is inferred from the structure and cited literature on RING mechanisms.

claim: The stimulated activity of RNF213 with UbcH7 was 2-3 times higher than with UbcH5 variants.
source: The stimulated activity was in this case even 2–3 times higher than with UbcH5 variants, which are promiscuous E2 enzymes working with many E3 ligases (Figure 3c).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the E2 screen assay.

claim: UbcH5 variants are promiscuous E2 enzymes working with many E3 ligases.
source: The stimulated activity was in this case even 2–3 times higher than with UbcH5 variants, which are promiscuous E2 enzymes working with many E3 ligases (Figure 3c).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about UbcH5.

claim: UbcH7 lacks intrinsic reactivity with lysine.
source: This finding is surprising, because UbcH7 is not known to collaborate with canonical RING-type E3s as it lacks intrinsic reactivity with lysine.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about UbcH7.

claim: RNF213 outranks LUBAC, PARKIN, and HERC2 as a UbcH7-collaborating E3 ligase in proteomics analysis.
source: Using an activity-based E2 probe, RNF213 was identified as one of the most prominent E3 ligases collaborating with UbcH7, outranking its established partner enzymes, such as LUBAC, PARKIN, and HERC2.
evidence: This is cited from a published proteomics study.

claim: A previous analysis claimed a critical role of the RING for the ubiquitination reaction.
source: These data contrast with a previous analysis claiming a critical role of the RING for the ubiquitination reaction (Liu et al., 2011).
evidence: This is cited from a previous publication.

claim: The previous analysis used a deletion far beyond the RING domain (corresponding to Δ3947-4042 in mouse RNF213) that presumably disrupted the E3 fold.
source: However, that analysis was carried out with a deletion far beyond the RING domain (corresponding to Δ3947–4042 in mouse RNF213) that presumably disrupted the E3 fold, highlighting the value of precise structural information for performing detailed mechanistic analyses.
evidence: This is inferred by comparing the previous deletion with the current structural information.

claim: RNF213 employs a yet undescribed E3 scaffold to perform its ubiquitin ligase function in a RING-independent manner.
source: The active ΔRING mutant therefore shares no similarity to any known E3 ligase either on the sequence or on the structural level, suggesting that RNF213 employs a yet undescribed E3 scaffold to perform its ubiquitin ligase function in a RING-independent manner.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural and functional data.

claim: More than 2% of the East Asian population carry disease-associated mutations in RNF213.
source: More than 2% of the East Asian population carry disease-associated mutations in RNF213.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as epidemiological information.

claim: Recent work revealed the involvement of RNF213 in hypoxia, lipid metabolism, NF-κB signalling, and angiogenesis.
source: Upon addressing its pathologic role in MDD, recent work revealed the involvement RNF213 in hypoxia, lipid metabolism, NF-κB signalling, and angiogenesis (Banh et al., 2016; Piccolis et al., 2019; Sugihara et al., 2019).
evidence: This is cited from recent publications on RNF213 function.

claim: RNF213 combines AAA ATPase and E3 activities in a single polypeptide, yielding a unique ubiquitination machine.
source: Moreover, it was shown that RNF213 combines AAA ATPase and E3 activities in a single polypeptide (Kamada et al., 2011), yielding a unique ubiquitination machine in the ubiquitin-proteasome system.
evidence: This is cited from a previous publication.

claim: The absence of structural counterparts to the E3 module subdomains in the PDB database highlights the distinct architecture of the RNF213 ubiquitin ligase.
source: The absence of structural counterparts to the E3 module subdomains in the PDB database apart from the RING domain highlights the distinct architecture of the RNF213 ubiquitin ligase.
evidence: This is inferred from the DALI search results.

claim: RNF213 belongs to the dynein ATPase family.
source: One of the most remarkable features discovered by the cryo-EM analysis is that RNF213 belongs to the dynein ATPase family, encoding six AAA units in a single polypeptide.
evidence: This is based on structural comparison with dynein.

claim: RNF213 is most similar to the resting states of dynein, in which the AAA ring is also open.
source: Structural alignments indicated that RNF213 is most similar to the resting states of dynein, in which the AAA ring is also open (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on structural alignment with dynein structures.

claim: RNF213 features two highly conserved loops in the AAA ring, presumably controlling the ATPase activity of AAA3 and AAA4.
source: Moreover, RNF213 features two highly conserved loops in the AAA ring, presumably controlling the ATPase activity of the two functional AAA3 and AAA4 units.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural positions and conservation of IR3 and IR5.

claim: RNF213 does not represent a processive ATPase.
source: We thus propose that RNF213 does not represent a processive ATPase, as would be required for example for it to use its AAA ring to promote the remodeling of E3 target proteins.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of an active AAA1 and low ATPase activity.

claim: The distribution of active/inactive ATPase sites in RNF213 points to a regulated switch promoting conformational changes by opening and closing the AAA ring.
source: The distribution of active/inactive ATPase sites rather point to a regulated switch promoting conformational changes by opening and closing the AAA ring, of which the first state is depicted in the present study.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural features of the AAA ring.

claim: The ribosome maturation factor Rea1 was observed in an auto-inhibited form stabilized by a specific insertion into AAA2.
source: Interestingly, the ribosome maturation factor Rea1 – another six AAA-domain containing protein with structural homology to RNF213 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1) – was also observed in an auto-inhibited form that is stabilized by a specific insertion into AAA2 (Chen et al., 2018; Sosnowski et al., 2018).
evidence: This is cited from published studies on Rea1.

claim: In Rea1, certain cofactors promote the release of the inhibitory element, unlocking the AAA hexamer.
source: In Rea1, certain cofactors promote the release of the inhibitory element, unlocking the AAA hexamer and inducing conformational changes required to interact with the C-terminal MIDAS domain, and subsequently with other ribosome assembly factors.
evidence: This is cited from published studies on Rea1 mechanism.

claim: The AAA switch in RNF213 could be transmitted to the C-terminal E3 module, regulating ubiquitination activity.
source: Given the similar overall organization of Rea1 and RNF213 (Figure 2—figure supplement 3), the AAA switch proposed for RNF213 could be analogously transmitted to the C-terminal E3 module, regulating ubiquitination activity.
evidence: This is inferred by analogy with Rea1 mechanism.

claim: RNF213 collaborates with UbcH7, a cysteine-reactive E2 enzyme typically stimulating ubiquitination activity of HECT and RBR E3 ligases.
source: To characterize the E3 function of RNF213, we used auto-ubiquitination as a proxy readout for its catalytic activity. Our data demonstrate that RNF213 collaborates with UbcH7, a cysteine-reactive E2 enzyme typically stimulating ubiquitination activity of HECT and RBR E3 ligases.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the E2 screen and auto-ubiquitination assays.

claim: RNF213 does not depend on its RING domain to function as an E3 ubiquitin ligase.
source: Moreover, we observed that RNF213 does not depend on its naming RING domain to function as an E3 ubiquitin ligase.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the functional activity of the ΔRING mutant.

claim: The modified UbcH7 ABP exhibited the same cross-linking activity with RNF213 as the unmodified ABP.
source: Contrary to RBR enzymes, the modified UbcH7 ABP exhibited the same cross-linking activity with RNF213 as the unmodified ABP (Pao et al., 2018).
evidence: This is cited from a published proteomics study.

claim: The RING-less RNF213 exhibits strong auto-ubiquitination activity.
source: Strikingly, the RING-less RNF213, which exhibits strong auto-ubiquitination activity, does not display structural similarity to any of the known ubiquitination enzyme in eukaryotes nor to the novel E3-like ligases (NEL, Maculins et al., 2016) that are found in bacterial pathogens and also operate in a RING-independent manner.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the auto-ubiquitination assay of the ΔRING mutant.

claim: Novel E3-like ligases (NEL) are found in bacterial pathogens and operate in a RING-independent manner.
source: Strikingly, the RING-less RNF213, which exhibits strong auto-ubiquitination activity, does not display structural similarity to any of the known ubiquitination enzyme in eukaryotes nor to the novel E3-like ligases (NEL, Maculins et al., 2016) that are found in bacterial pathogens and also operate in a RING-independent manner.
evidence: This is cited from published literature on NEL enzymes.

claim: RNF213 is the founding member of a distinct class of E3 ligases employing a Cys-containing motif.
source: We thus propose that RNF213 is the founding member of a distinct class of E3 ligases, employing a Cys-containing motif similarly as HECT, RBR, and RCR enzymes, but utilizing a distinct structural scaffold to promote the ubiquitin transfer.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural and functional data.

claim: The findings highlight the unexplored mechanistic diversity within the ubiquitination network.
source: Although the E3 mechanism, the identity of the active site cysteine and the role of the RING domain remain to be resolved, our findings highlight the unexplored mechanistic diversity within the ubiquitination network.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the novel findings about RNF213.

claim: The majority of MMD mutations with a high pathology CADD score cluster in the composite E3 module.
source: Remarkably, the majority of the MMD mutations with a high pathology CADD score cluster in the composite E3 module, affecting each of the four sub-domains.
evidence: This is based on mapping MMD mutations onto the structure and analyzing CADD scores.

claim: MMD mutations interfere with the ubiquitination activity of RNF213, leading to either mechanistic inhibition or altered substrate binding.
source: These data suggest that MMD mutations interfere with the ubiquitination activity of RNF213, leading to either mechanistic inhibition or altered substrate binding.
evidence: This is inferred from the clustering of mutations in the E3 module.

claim: The cryo-EM structure provides a precise roadmap to dissect the role of RNF213 in vascular formation and Moyamoya disease.
source: The presented cryo-EM structure now provides a precise roadmap to dissect the role of RNF213 in vascular formation and the connected Moyamoya disease.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the utility of the structural information.
